Before
 Hon'Ble Shri Justice Pavan Kumar Dwivedi

 Misc. Appeal No. 3761 of 2018
 Smt. Shajiya And Others
 Versus
 Sabir Khan And Others
 Appearance:
 Shri Romil Malpani - Advocate for the appellants.
Shri Sudhir Dandwate, learned counsel for the responde  ORDER 1.

The appellants have filed this appeal under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, being aggrieved by the award dated 22/6/2018 passed by the IIIrd Addl. Member MACT, Distt. Dhar in Claim Case No.236/2017, challenging the quantum of compensation.

entities.text: IIIrd Addl. Member MACT, Distt. Dhar
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. The factum of accident and liability of Insurance Company are not in dispute.
3. The short facts giving rise to the case are that on 15/12/2013 around 6.30 PM deceased Mustafa Parvez Siddique was going on a bike along with his friends Mohammed Shabbir and Mubarik.
Friends of the deceased were coming behind the motorcycle of deceased Mustafa Parvez on a separate motorcycle.

At around 6.30 PM when they reached between the village Amalpur and Bhavsinghpura, on Khandwa Harda road a bus having registration No.M.P. 13 P. 0570 came from the side of Khandwa which was NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:16985 2 MA-3761-2018 being driven by the respondent No.1 driver in a very rash and negligent manner.
He came on the wrong side of the road and dashed into the motorcycle of Mustafa Parvez because of which he sustained grievous injuries on his head, face, abdomen and chest.
His motorcycle was also completely broken.
He was immediately rushed by ambulance to Government Hospital, Khandwa where the doctors declared him dead.
4 . The appellants have filed claim petition under Section 166 of the M.V. Act, claiming compensation for the death of Mustafa Parvez Siddique due to above said accident.
The claims tribunal after considering the evidence on record awarded an amount of Rs.5,57,000/- in all heads to the appellants.

Counsel for the appellants submits that the claims tribunal has not considered the evidence as rendered by the appellants regarding the income of the deceased in its proper perspective.
He submits that the claims tribunal has discarded the evidence of witness Abhishek (AW.5) who deposed before the tribunal that he is a Branch Manager in Dena Bank Branch, Dhar.
He stated that he has been authorized by Zonal Office, Bhopal for deposing in the present claim case.
He stated that deceased Mustafa Parvez Siddiquie had obtained bank loan of Rs.10,00,000/-.
The bank had disbursed him Rs.9,50,000/-, which was given for centering work.
The said witness also stated that the EMI for the said loan was Rs.12,500/- per month.
He further stated that the entire amount was repaid by the deceased.
In support of the same Exhibit P/9 was produced which was a letter from Madhya Pradesh Khadi Gram Udyog.

Other documents regarding loan were Exhibits P/8, P/10 to P/14 which included application form, training letter, caste certificate, NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-IND:16985 3 MA-3761-2018 bank statement and notice.

Counsel states that in view of undeniable evidence which was before the claims tribunal the findings recorded by it in para 26 to the effect that the income of the deceased was not proved and thus taking the income of the deceased at Rs.3,350/- per month by treating him skilled labour is not proper.
He further submits that no future prospects have been added in the income of the deceased.
In view of the same he submits that the amount of compensation is very meager and is totally unacceptable in view of the clear evidence brought on record by the appellants / claimants.
6. Learned counsel for respondent No.3 / Insurance Company on the other hand has supported the findings of the claims tribunal by referring to the findings of para 36 of the impugned award.

Counsel stated that in absence of any document to show that the deceased was a contractor or property broker the tribunal has correctly discarded the claim of the appellant regarding the income of the deceased and has correctly taken the income of the deceased on notional basis at Rs.3,350/-.

He also submits that as the claim relates to the accident occurred on 15/12/2013 thus the tribunal correctly has not added anything in future prospects.
7.
Heard the learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.

8. The conclusions drawn by the claims tribunal in para 25 and 26 of the impugned award are not sustainable in view of the documents enclosed as Exhibits P/9 to P/15 as well as the statement of witness Abhishek (A.W.5) who was the Branch Manager of Dena Bank.
Exhibit P/8 is the bank statement of the loan account of the deceased Mustafa Parvez Siddiquie.
He NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:16985 4 MA-3761-2018 had obtained the loan of Rs.10,00,000/- for which he was paying EMI of Rs.12,500/-.

It is further seen from Exhibit P/9 that he had undergone an entrepreneurship development programme under the P.M.E.G.P. of the Ministry of Micro Small and Medium Enterprises (MSME) of the Government of India.

entities.text: Ministry of Micro Small and Medium Enterprises (MSME)
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Page 52 of Exhibit P/9 is a letter issued by the Assistant Manager of M.P. Khadi and Gram Udhyog Board issued to Bank Manager of Dena Bank asking for change of business activity from Jewellery making to centering work.
Next is the documents Exhibit P/10, which is a form of M.P. Khadi Gram Udhyog Board where the deceased had applied for employment in the year 2012-13.
It is thus clear that the deceased was not unemployed person but has actively pursuing his career and was sanctioned a loan of Rs.10,00,000/-.
The bank disbursed Rs.9,50,000/- to him and he was regularly paying EMI of Rs.12,500/- for the repayment of the said loan.

V/s. United India Insurance Co. Ltd & Ors. reported as 2023 ACJ 279 has held in para 8 and 9 as under :-
"8.

entities.text: United India Insurance Co. Ltd & Ors. reported as 2023 ACJ 279
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Though, there is no evidence on record regarding the income of deceased Pyara Singh, however, from the testimony of P.W.4 - Amar Kumar, Assistant Manager,
Kotak Mahindra Bank Limited, it is clear that the deceased - Pyara Singh was regularly making the payment of Rs.11,550/- as installment to discharge his loan liability towards the tractor.
At this rate, the entire loan was paid back within a year or so.
That clearly establishes the earning capacity of the deceased.
It is also the case of the appellants-claimants that the deceased was working as a contractor and was earning Rs.50,000/- per month.
In our considered view, the Tribunal's approach is quite justified in law as well as on facts.

In the summary proceedings where the approach of the NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:16985 5 MA-3761-2018 Tribunal's determination must be in conformity with the object of the welfare legislation, it was rightly held that the monthly income of the deceased could not be less than Rs.25,000/-.The reason assigned by the High Court to reduce the monthly income of the deceased is totally cryptic and has no rationale.
The Notification of Minimum Wages Act can be a guiding factor only in a case where there is no clue available to evaluate monthly income of the deceased.
Where positive evidence has been led, no reliance on the Notification could be placed, particularly when it was nobody's case that the deceased was a labourer as presumed by the High Court."
9 . However there is a difference in this case.
It is seen from the bank statement Exhibit P/8 that subsidy of Rs.3,50,000/- has also been provided to deceased on 10/9/2014 under some scheme of the Central Government.
The date of accident is 15/12/2013.
Thus in the present case solely based on the bank statement it cannot be concluded that the appellant was earning Rs.12,500/- or more in each month.
It is clear that he has taken initial steps for starting his work and was settling his feet in the business.

Thus in the given peculiar facts of this case, it would be appropriate to treat the deceased as an entrepreneur who was beginning his career and thus he has to be placed above the skilled labour category.
For skilled labour category at the relevant time the minimum wages were around Rs.5800/- per month.
Thus in the fitness of things it would be appropriate to take the income of the deceased at Rs.8000/- per month.
The multiplier as applied by the claims tribunal at 15 is correct.

In view of the law as laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of National Insurance Company Ltd. Vs. Pranay Sethi and Others 2017 (16) SCC 680, addition of 40% in the income of the deceased has to be made taking into consideration his age at 39 years and looking to Smt. As such the total amount of compensation for loss of dependency would come to Rs.15,12,000/-.

As there are four claimants thus an amount of Rs.40,000/- each is to be awarded, NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-IND:16985 6 MA-3761-2018 for all of them it would come to Rs.1,60,000/- and for funeral and loss of estate an amount of Rs.30,000/- is to be awarded.
Thus the total compensation would come to Rs.17,02,000/-.

The claims tribunal has already awarded an amount of Rs.5,47,000/- after deducting the same, the appellant are held entitled for payment of Rs.11,55,000/- over and above what has already been awarded by the claims tribunal.
The enhanced amount of compensation shall carry interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of filing of the claim application before the claims tribunal.
1 0 . It is seen from the record that the appeal has been valued at Rs.10,00,000/-.
Thus the appellants are required to pay deficit Court fee within a period of one month from today.
11. With the aforesaid, the appeal stands allowed and disposed off.

(PAVAN KUMAR DWIVEDI) JUDGE SS/-
